title: A Fading Life and a Lasting God
overview: A person who feels their life wasting away pours out their pain, then takes comfort that the LORD lasts forever and will restore ruined Jerusalem.

parts.label: A cry to be heard (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The heading in Hebrew Bibles calls this the prayer of a worn-out sufferer pouring out a complaint. Asking God not to hide his face means asking God not to turn away or seem absent in a time of trouble.

parts.label: Wasting away (vv. 3-11)
parts.note: Smoke, burning bones, withered grass and a lone bird on a rooftop picture someone sick, sleepless and cut off, while enemies use his name as a curse. Eating ashes was a sign of mourning, and he openly blames God's anger, saying God picked him up only to throw him down.

parts.label: God reigns, Zion will rise (vv. 12-17)
parts.note: The mood turns: the speaker's days are short, but the LORD rules forever and will have mercy on Zion, meaning Jerusalem. Loving the city's stones and dust suggests it lay in ruins, and many scholars link this to the time after Babylon destroyed it, though the date is uncertain.

parts.label: A message for later (vv. 18-22)
parts.note: The speaker wants this hope written down so people not yet born will praise God for hearing prisoners and those facing death. These captives may be Israel's exiles, and the picture widens to whole nations gathering to worship.

parts.label: Short life, endless God (vv. 23-28)
parts.note: Feeling cut off in midlife, he contrasts himself with God, who made earth and sky and will outlast them the way someone replaces worn-out clothes. Christians later read verses 25 to 27 as describing Jesus, because the New Testament letter to the Hebrews applies them to him.

disagreement: Readers differ on whether the sufferer is mainly one sick individual, a voice for the whole people in exile, or, as some Christians hold because of Hebrews, a figure pointing ahead to Christ.
think: When life feels fragile or short, does the thought of something that outlasts you bring comfort, frustration, or something else entirely?
